messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Streaming disconnects for enterprise customer AtlasBank affecting dedicated-vpc-nyc pool. Symptoms: websocket streams cut after ~25-35s, client sees 502/connection_reset. Error rate spiked to 18% for /v1/stream (avg 0.4%). Paging on-call.

maya: I'm the current on-call. Paging SRE rotation, taking initial triage. Assigning @sam to lead.

sam: I'm on it. Can someone paste a representative client error and a proxy log tail? Any recent config deploys to the nyc dedicated pool?

jess: Customer support (jess): Atlas reported first incident at 2026-03-15T10:05Z. They reported intermittent disconnects from their app gateway; they see ECONNRESET or 502 after ~30s. Attachments: traces and a short pcap (sent to eng). No config changes on their side reported.

leo: eng-runtime: we had a rolling nginx-proxy change 3h ago to increase upstream keepalive but only targeted hosted pool. Dedicated-vpc-nyc wasn't touched by that rollout. No runtime code deploys in last 24h.

sam: OK. Pulling logs now. Suspect: idle websocket/ping/pong mismatch between customer gateway and our ingress LB. Seeing repeated "upstream prematurely closed connection" in proxy logs.

sam: log excerpt: ```
[10:12:03] proxy_1 | 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.45, server: stream.redwood.internal, request: "GET /v1/stream?model=redwood-3 HTTP/1.1"
[10:12:03] proxy_1 | 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z 502 while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.45, server: stream.redwood.internal
```

leo: Also seeing intermittent "write timeout" in worker logs around the same time: ```
2026-03-15T10:12:02.987Z worker-7 ERROR ws: write timeout after 30000ms
```

sam: That matches client ~30s. Two hypotheses: 1) LB idle timeout shorter than customer's retry/keepalive; 2) our gateway is closing idle streams when request token usage spikes and eviction triggers.

oliver: acct-eng: I'm on the line with Atlas support now. They say they have aggressive client reconnects and custom retry logic that hits our pool fast. Impact: live streaming for 12% of their sessions, business-critical telemetry lost for their fraud detection path. They're asking for immediate mitigation.

jess: Customer impact: 1) user-facing streaming degraded, falling back to polling at higher latency; 2) potential SLA credit request.

sam: Immediate mitigation options (we should choose in next 5-10m):
- Increase ingress LB timeout and proxy keepalive to 90s for dedicated-vpc-nyc.
- Apply temporary rate limit on Atlas tenant to reduce burst pressure and avoid worker eviction.
- Route Atlas traffic to a less-busy dedicated pool in eu-west as a fallback (requires customer approval and GDPR check).
- Enable short-term sticky connections (session pinning) to avoid proxy churn.

maya: Prioritize non-invasive fixes first. Sam, can you try bumping proxy keepalive + LB timeout for the dedicated-vpc-nyc and monitor? If that doesn't help, we fall back to imposing a token/burst limit on their tenant.

sam: Applying proxy keepalive change now for vpc-nyc (hot patch): updating nginx upstream config to set proxy_read_timeout 90s; proxy_send_timeout 90s; keepalive_timeout 90s. Pushing config to subset of frontends to test (canary 10%). Deploy-bot will report.

deploy-bot: Rolling config change to frontend-proxy-nyc: canary 10% (cfg id cfg-nyc-20260315-1).

sam: Canary finished; monitoring logs and error rate. Initial drop in 502s on canary hosts. Applying to remaining frontends in 3m.

leo: Also adding a runtime guard: limit simultaneous websocket accept per-worker to avoid KV eviction storms. Pushing a conservative change to runtime config (no code change).

sam: Full rollout done. Error rate for Atlas traffic dropped from 18% -> 3% over 6 minutes. Latency stable.

oliver: I'll update Atlas: we've applied a configuration change on our ingress to increase keepalive and timeout which should stop premature disconnects. Asking them to validate on their end.

jess: Atlas confirms improvement on their staging gateway. They want to test production for 30m then we'll decide on permanent fix.

maya: Assessment: root cause appears to be mismatch between proxy/LB timeouts and customer gateway keepalive/retry behavior combined with sudden concentrated burst from Atlas tenant. Dedicated pool was sensitive because of local worker limits. No code regression identified.

sam: Next steps (short-term):
- Keep proxy timeouts at 90s for dedicated-vpc-nyc for 24h.
- Put a temporary tenant-level burst cap for Atlas: max concurrent streams 400 (rollback if customer objects).
- Schedule follow-up with eng-runtime to tune accept/backpressure behavior and add telemetry for ping/pong latencies.

leo: Long-term: add tenant-aware autoscale for dedicated pools, improve graceful eviction to prefer new accepts over old idle streams, expose per-tenant stream limits in console.

oliver: Customer comms: propose a post-incident call at 1600Z to review timeline and proposed permanent mitigations.

jess: Logging ticket created: INC-2026-4543 (follow-up: add ping/pong metrics, add SLO dashboard for streaming errors).

maya: On-call handoff: Sam will remain lead for next 2 hours. I'll mark the incident as mitigated once Atlas validates production and error rate <1% for 20m.

sam: Monitoring shows steady state ~0.8% for Atlas prod for last 12 minutes. Will continue to watch.

maya: Thanks team. Keep the thread updated for the 1600Z postmortem invite. Closing paging; incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
